root.label: Object layout and alignment
root.note: The standard guarantees relationships; the ABI supplies the actual numbers.

children.label: Size and alignment
children.note: Every complete type has a size and a power-of-two alignment.

children.label: sizeof multiple of alignof
children.note: Arrays have no gaps and every element is aligned, so size is a multiple of alignment.

children.label: Fundamental sizes
children.note: Character types are size 1; bool, int, pointers and the rest are implementation-defined.

children.label: Over-alignment
children.note: alignas raises alignment; since C++17 new uses align_val_t overloads for extended alignment.

children.label: Member order and padding
children.note: Members sit at increasing addresses in declaration order, with padding for alignment.

children.label: C++23 order rule
children.note: P1847: declaration order holds regardless of access control; before C++23 only within one access level.

children.label: Sort by alignment
children.note: The compiler never reorders members, so sorting by decreasing alignment shrinks padding.

children.label: Class properties
children.note: Properties that decide what you may do with an object's bytes.

children.label: Trivially copyable
children.note: Eligible copy/move ops all trivial plus trivial destructor; enables memcpy and bit_cast.

children.label: Standard-layout
children.note: No virtuals, uniform member access, members in one class; enables offsetof and C compatibility.

children.label: POD is deprecated
children.note: Trivial plus standard-layout; std::is_pod was deprecated in C++20.

children.label: Empty subobjects
children.note: Complete empty objects have nonzero size, but subobjects may overlap others.

children.label: Empty base optimization
children.note: An empty base subobject may occupy zero bytes.

children.label: [[no_unique_address]]
children.note: C++20: members may overlap like bases; MSVC ignores it and needs [[msvc::no_unique_address]].

children.label: Distinct address rule
children.note: Two objects of the same type never share an address, so same-type empties cannot overlap each other.

children.label: Bit-fields and ABI
children.note: The parts of layout the standard leaves to the implementation.

children.label: Bit-field allocation
children.note: Unit size, straddling and bit order are implementation-defined; no address or sizeof.

children.label: One memory location
children.note: Adjacent nonzero-width bit-fields form one memory location; a :0 field starts a new one.

children.label: Vtables are ABI
children.note: Itanium puts the vptr at offset 0 and virtual bases last; the standard never mentions vtables.

children.label: offsetof limits
children.note: Use on non-standard-layout types is conditionally-supported since C++17.

children.label: Representations
children.note: Object representation is all sizeof(T) bytes; value representation is the bits that matter.

children.label: Padding bits
children.note: Not part of the value; member-wise init leaves them unspecified, zero-initialization clears them.

children.label: Unique representations
children.note: has_unique_object_representations (C++17) is false with padding and typically for floats.
